papers.title: Large Scale Variable Fidelity Surrogate Modeling
papers.abstract: Engineers widely use Gaussian process regression framework to construct surrogate models aimed to replace computationally expensive physical models while exploring design space. Thanks to Gaussian process properties we can use both samples generated by a high fidelity function (an expensive and accurate representation of a physical phenomenon) and a low fidelity function (a cheap and coarse approximation of the same physical phenomenon) while constructing a surrogate model. However, if samples sizes are more than few thousands of points, computational costs of the Gaussian process regression become prohibitive both in case of learning and in case of prediction calculation. We propose two approaches to circumvent this computational burden: one approach is based on the Nyström approximation of sample covariance matrices and another is based on an intelligent usage of a blackbox that can evaluate a~low fidelity function on the fly at any point of a design space. We examine performance of the proposed approaches using a number of artificial and real problems, including engineering optimization of a rotating disk shape.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了大规模变保真度代理模型方法，可转移到生物力学植入物设计领域，但缺少生物医学上下文验证。
llm.why_not_core: No biomedical context or implant-specific constraints; the method is demonstrated on general engineering optimization of a rotating disk, not on biomechanics or implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 降低变保真度代理模型在大样本下的计算成本
summary_zh.method: 采用Nyström近似和在线低保真度评估两种方法加速高斯过程
summary_zh.result: 所提方法在样本量巨大时仍保持可扩展性
summary_zh.validation: 通过人工问题和旋转盘优化实例验证

summary_en.motivation: To reduce computational burden of Gaussian process-based multi-fidelity surrogate models when training sample sizes exceed thousands of points.
summary_en.method: Two scalable approaches are proposed: Nyström approximation of covariance matrices and an online low-fidelity evaluation blackbox that avoids pre-computed training sets.
summary_en.result: The proposed methods maintain predictive accuracy while drastically reducing learning and prediction time for large datasets.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on synthetic benchmarks and a real engineering design optimization of a rotating disk.

papers.title: Recall and patient perceptions of hip precautions 6 weeks after total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background and purpose - There is a lack of evidence to support the role of hip precautions in preventing dislocation following total hip arthroplasty (THA). We report an exploratory study which assesses recall, adherence, and the impact of precautions on activities of daily living in the first 6 weeks postoperatively. Patients and methods - We designed a new questionnaire based on the education patients receive and refined by professionals within our multidisciplinary team. 129 patients underwent primary elective THA during the study period and received the questionnaire at 6 weeks postoperatively. Results - 97 (75%) patients responded before the 8th week postoperatively. Most of these (83 patients) could remember all the precautions. Of the 97 who responded only 22 claimed to adhere to all of the precautions. 48 admitted to putting their own underwear on without the use of aids or assistance, and 38 had started walking without an aid. Due to the precautions 67 avoided leaving the house at some point and 63 were unable to perform desired activities. 84 stated that their sleep was affected. There were no dislocations among the 97 patients who responded; however, there was 1 dislocation among the 32 non-responders. Interpretation - We found that most patients did not adhere to hip precaution advice. Precautions have a detrimental effect on patient activity and sleep. In view of the limited efficacy in reducing dislocation rate, we question the use of precautions in the primary arthroplasty setting.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究全髋关节置换术后患者对髋部预防措施的回忆和依从性，未涉及任何生物力学建模或植入物设计。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not quantify stress shielding, micromotion, or implant stability, nor does it include any finite element analysis or contact mechanics; it is purely a clinical survey on postoperative patient behavior.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估全髋关节置换术后患者对髋部预防措施的回忆和依从性
summary_zh.method: 设计问卷调查，术后6周对129名患者进行调查
summary_zh.result: 仅少数患者遵守预防措施，且预防措施影响日常活动和睡眠
summary_zh.validation: 问卷回收率和患者自我报告数据

summary_en.motivation: To assess patient recall, adherence, and impact of hip precautions after total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A questionnaire was designed and administered to 129 primary THA patients at 6 weeks postoperatively.
summary_en.result: Most patients did not adhere to all precautions, which negatively affected daily activities and sleep, with no dislocations reported in respondents.
summary_en.validation: Survey responses from 97 out of 129 patients (75% response rate).
